findingStatement: Saffire-I established steady-state concurrent flame spread of ~2.4 mm/s over a large-scale SIBAL fabric panel (40.6 cm x 94 cm) in microgravity under 20 cm/s air flow in nominal cabin air (21.5% O2, 101.3 kPa).
applicableConditions: Concurrent forced airflow 20 cm/s, Cygnus cabin atmosphere (101.3 kPa, 21.5% O2)
limitations: Tested only at 20 cm/s forced flow; dynamic spread rates were derived from video pyrometry analysis, not recorded in the PSI specimen table.

findingStatement: Saffire-I combustion of PMMA produced a concurrent flame spread rate of ~0.18 mm/s, demonstrating that non-charring thermoplastic PMMA propagates an order of magnitude slower than thin cellulosic/fiberglass SIBAL fabric.
applicableConditions: Cygnus cabin nominal (101.3 kPa, 21% O2, 20 cm/s flow)
limitations: PMMA sample was thick card configuration; direct scaling to thin PMMA films requires correcting for thermal Biot number.

findingStatement: Saffire-I combustion generated a transient pressure rise of Delta P approx 0.5 kPa within the Cygnus vehicle cargo volume.
applicableConditions: Cygnus pressurized module (sealed volume approx 19 m^3)
limitations: Pressure spike depends on vehicle sealed volume to burn area ratio; cannot be scaled linearly to larger ISS modules without ventilation modeling.

findingStatement: In BASS-II, opposed-flow flame spread over cylindrical PMMA rods showed low-speed radiative quenching below approximately 1.5 cm/s, exhibiting a non-monotonic flammability boundary.
applicableConditions: Microgravity Science Glovebox, cylindrical PMMA rods (dia 6.35 - 12.7 mm)
limitations: Pertains to thick cylindrical PMMA rods in opposed flow; DOES NOT apply directly to thin PMMA films (Bhattacharjee series, PSI25-ART-002) which lack axial stagnation flow.

findingStatement: BASS-II Bhattacharjee test series mapped flame spread over thin PMMA films (100, 200, 300 micron) in a small flow duct with discrete fan display settings (47 to 62).
applicableConditions: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox nominal air, uncalibrated flow indices
limitations: Fan display setting is an integer dial (47-62); true flow velocity in cm/s is uncalibrated without duct calibration curves.

findingStatement: FLEX demonstrated that isolated alkane droplets burning in quiescent microgravity extinguish radiatively at large finite diameters (d_ext), and can transition into low-temperature cool-flame combustion without visible radiation.
sourcePublication: Dietrich et al., Combust. Flame (2017) / Nayagam et al. (2015)
limitations: FLEX experimental records are DEFERRED from FIRELINE's currently indexed dataset; liquid droplet evaporation mechanics cannot be used as empirical evidence for solid fuel spread.

findingStatement: Solid fuel flame spread is fundamentally non-comparable across divergent fuel geometries: thin films (BASS-II, Bi << 0.1) pyrolyze uniformly through thickness, whereas thick rods (Olson, Bi > 1) are governed by surface heat conduction, and SIBAL composite fabrics retain a porous fiberglass char scaffold.
limitations: Prohibits direct quantitative cross-geometry extrapolation without thermal Biot number adjustments.

findingStatement: There is a complete empirical evidence gap for solid materials flammability in reduced partial gravity (Lunar 0.16g and Martian 0.38g). NASA PSI flight archives contain microgravity (10^-6 g) and ground 1g data, but partial-gravity transition boundaries remain untested in long-duration flight.
limitations: Zero flight combustion data exists in current repository for partial gravity.

findingStatement: There is a major empirical evidence gap for materials flammability under Exploration Atmospheres (34% O2 at 56.5 kPa / 8.2 psia). Saffire-I and BASS-II tested strictly in nominal sea-level cabin air (21% O2 at 101.3 kPa).
limitations: Existing Saffire-I and BASS-II flight data CANNOT predict flammability or extinction limits in 34% O2 exploration habitats.
